Subject: Custom availability exhibit & latency note for our MSA

Hi Lauren,

We're progressing toward signature on the MSA but our procurement and compliance teams are asking for two items to be attached to the agreement before sign: an explicit 'Availability Exhibit' that calls out uptime / latency commitments for the clinical inference workload, and a short paragraph for the order form that grants an availability exception for planned maintenance windows over major release rollouts.

Key asks from our side: 
- Target uptime SLA expressed as monthly uptime percentage and credit mechanism for breaches.
- Average 95th-percentile inference tail latency target for p95 (50 tokens) and definition of measurement window.
- Clear description of the exception for scheduled upgrades (max duration per upgrade event, notification window).

We can accept standard credit language, but we need the exception to be explicit because our clinical workflows have blackout windows where capacity shifts are risky. Can you share a draft exhibit and the order form language you propose? Also include any SOC/Security attestation that supports uptime guarantees.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-min call if useful.

James —

Thanks for the clear list. We've drafted an "Availability Exhibit" (attached) and a short Order Form paragraph that codifies: monthly uptime percentage, the credit ladder, p95 latency measurement for a 50-token baseline, and a scheduled-maintenance exception with notification windows. Highlights: 

- Proposed uptime: 99.9% monthly (with credits tiered at 99.0% and 99.5%).
- Latency: p95 <= 220ms for 50-token gen on the reserved-dedicated pool; measurement window defined as system-side token completion timestamps aggregated UTC per calendar month.
- Scheduled maintenance: up to 3 maintenance events per calendar quarter, each up to 6 hours; 72-hour advance notification.

We also attached our current SOC 2 attestation for evidence. Please note the latency number above is for the Dedicated capacity profile we provisioned for MediVance; hosted/public model variants have higher tail latencies and we suggest routing clinical-critical requests to the dedicated pool.

Next steps I propose: 
1) Review the attached Exhibit + Order Form draft and mark any items you want softened or tightened.
2) If you agree, we can prepare a DocuSign envelope that includes both the MSA and the Exhibit as an attachment.
3) If you need stricter measurement language (rolling-window vs calendar-month), loop in your SRE & we'll have Karthik propose a technical clause.

I've cc'd Karthik and Stephanie — Karthik can confirm the measurement/metric language; Stephanie is on the CS side for operational runbooks and notifications.

Best,

James / Lauren —

Quick technical clarifications and suggested alternate language below that often helps avoid ambiguity between product and procurement teams: 

1) Measurement window: we recommend "calendar month, UTC" as the default, but add an option for a 30-day rolling window if MediVance needs smoothing across cutovers. Example clause: 
"Monthly Uptime" means the percentage of minutes in a calendar month during which the Dedicated Inference Pool is available to accept requests, excluding scheduled maintenance windows and force majeure events. Uptime is measured at the Redwood ingress endpoints and aggregated in UTC.

2) Latency definition: make clear it's p95 for successful completions only and specify token baseline and model variant. Example clause: 
"Tail Latency (p95)" is the 95th percentile of end-to-end request completion times for successful generation requests using the dedicated model variant specified in the Order Form, measured on a 50-token baseline and aggregated per calendar month. 

3) Exception mechanics: for major release rollouts where stateful KV migrations may extend maintenance, we can allow an additional discretionary maintenance window (up to 12 hours) once per year with 7 days' notice. We proposed that in the attached Exhibit as an optional clause.

4) Evidence: SOC 2 attestation and our availability reporting exports (monthly CSV) can be provided on request; however, audit-level logs and health-check exports are scoped to Dedicated customers under the Private deployment contract. If MediVance needs continuous deliverables, we can add a reporting cadence to the order form.

Marcus: please confirm the 6-hour per-event cap and the one-time annual discretionary 12-hour migration allowance in the Exhibit are operationally feasible.

Happy to review language on a quick call if that helps finalize.

—Karthik

Director, Product Ops — Inference Platform
